mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS tightening is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE and corporate cost inflation is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past 3 months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past 2 months signals a weakening supply side, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO decline and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the past month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS growth and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 3 months signals strong demand in the housing market, which boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST growth and S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% over the past 6 months signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to monetary easing and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if accompanied by a decrease in the federal funds rate.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 decline and FEDFUNDS decrease is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during a late-cycle phase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of INDPRO decline and UNRATE increase on S&P 500 returns is not significant (p > 0.05).
